parsed.summary: This paper introduces a topological framework for analyzing and steering large language models (LLMs) in handling ill-posed questions. By treating prompt-token hidden states as point clouds and analyzing their topology using persistent homology, the authors derive seven descriptors to classify ill-posedness and guide model responses. Empirical evaluations demonstrate improved classification and steering performance across multiple datasets and LLM families.

chk_problem.value: Ill-posed questions pose challenges for LLMs due to ambiguity, under-specification, or conflicting statements.
chk_problem.paper_quote: Ill-posed questions, including those involving ambiguity, under-specification, or conflicting statements, may admit no valid answer or multiple plausible answers, posing a significant challenge for large language models (LLMs) despite their otherwise strong performance.

chk_method.value: A topology-based framework using persistent homology to analyze and steer LLM responses to ill-posed questions.
chk_method.paper_quote: We propose a topology-based framework for analyzing ill-posed questions and steering LLM responses.

chk_data.value: AmbigQA for binary detection and CLAMBER for nine-way classification of ill-posedness.
chk_data.paper_quote: Evaluation on AmbigQA for binary ill-posedness detection, and on CLAMBER for fine-grained 9-way ill-posedness classification demonstrates the effectiveness of the proposed topological representation.

chk_setup.value: Evaluation on eight open-weight models from four families using five split seeds and 70/10/20 train/validation/test splits.
chk_setup.paper_quote: We evaluate eight models from four families using five split seeds (0–4), with 70/10/20 train/validation/test splits.

chk_primary_result.value: 78.60% macro-F1 on AmbigQA binary detection and 39.44% macro-F1 on CLAMBER nine-way classification.
chk_primary_result.paper_quote: Across eight open-weight models from the Llama, Qwen, Gemma, and Ministral families, our seven H0 and H1 descriptors from a single selected layer improve average macro-F1 score over the strongest baselines from 75.51% to 78.60% on AmbigQA, and from 36.64% to 39.44% on CLAMBER 9-way classification.

chk_secondary_result.value: Topology-conditioned steering improved steered abstention response rate from 27.43% to 51.15%.
chk_secondary_result.paper_quote: Averaged across the four dataset–model settings, topology-conditioned steering improves steered abstention response rate from 27.43% to 51.15%.

chk_baseline.value: Compared against AEN and prompt-based baselines like few-shot and chain-of-thought prompting.
chk_baseline.paper_quote: We compare against AEN (Zhang et al., 2025), a probing baseline that selects ambiguity-predictive neurons and trains a classifier on their activations. Prompt-based comparisons include CLAMBER zero-shot (Zhang et al., 2024), CLAM few-shot (Kuhn et al., 2022), CLAMBER few-shot chain-of-thought (Zhang et al., 2024; Wei et al., 2022), and InfoGain prompting (Kim et al., 2024).

chk_conclusion.value: Compact token-cloud topology provides an effective representation and steering signal for ill-posed problems.
chk_conclusion.paper_quote: Together, these results demonstrate that compact token-cloud topology provides an effective, unified representation and steering signal for ill-posed problems.

chk_limitation.value: Incorrect detection or steering may cause unnecessary abstention or degraded responses.
chk_limitation.paper_quote: Incorrect detection or steering may cause unnecessary abstention or degraded responses.
